transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I'm a preschool teacher, and... what brings me in is that I have this really strong reaction to balloons. The second I spot them at school, even if they're just way across the hallway, my chest immediately tightens up. I kind of freeze for a moment before I can even think clearly about what I’m actually supposed to be doing. It's really becoming a problem for me at work.
Are there any other objects or situations that cause a similar reaction in you?
No, it's really just the balloons. I mean, I don't have this kind of reaction to anything else. It's just that one specific thing that really sets me off like that.
When you see balloons and your chest tightens up, what is it that you're afraid might happen?

Well, logically I know a balloon in the classroom is probably just a decoration. But... when I see one, especially if it looks stretched really tight or if it's bobbing around near the children, I just get this overwhelming feeling that it's going to burst right in my face. I get so scared, and I know it's... well, my reaction just seems way bigger than the actual situation calls for.
Did something happen to you in the past involving a balloon that might be connected to your current reaction?

Yeah, it actually did. Um, this whole thing has been going on for about seven months now. We were having a children’s art celebration at the preschool, and a balloon burst right close to my face. It really startled me, and... well, ever since that happened, I've just had this reaction.
When you think about the balloon bursting at the children's art celebration, do you feel anxious or scared?

Um, no, not really. I mean, just thinking about that day doesn't make me panic or anything. The memory itself is just... a memory. I don't get that scared, tight feeling in my chest just from remembering it. It really only happens when I'm actually in the room with a real balloon right in front of me.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain places or events because you think there might be balloons there?

Yeah, I definitely do. Um, especially at work. Lately, I've been asking my teaching aides to step in and handle the birthday circles. Or, you know, if we have a special event, I'll make sure to move away from any of the festival tables if there are balloons nearby. And if I absolutely have to stay in the area for the kids... well, I just keep my distance. I basically just focus on getting through it without looking at them.
Have you avoided any non-work-related activities or social gatherings because you thought there might be balloons present?

No, not really. Outside of work, I haven't really run into that issue. I don't usually go to places where there are balloons anyway, so I haven't had to avoid any personal events or anything like that. It's really just the preschool stuff where it comes up.
How much distress do you feel when you have to avoid balloons or events where balloons might be present at work?

It's pretty distressing, honestly. It has started affecting my work, which bothers me. I mean, having to hand off normal classroom celebrations to my aides isn't ideal. And recently, I actually missed helping out with a festival art table that I had spent time planning, just because there were balloons around it. My supervisor definitely noticed that I wasn't there, so... yeah, it's becoming a problem for my job.
Has your reaction to balloons affected your relationships with friends or family members in any way?

No, not really. Um, it hasn't caused any issues with my family or friends. Like I mentioned earlier, I don't really run into balloons in my personal life much anyway, so it hasn't gotten in the way of seeing them or caused any arguments. It's really just isolated to my job right now.
Are there any daily activities you've stopped doing or changed because of your fear of balloons?
No, not really. Outside of work, my daily routine hasn't changed at all. I still do all my normal errands and chores and everything. It's really just the classroom stuff that's been affected.
Have you ever avoided going to a store or a public place because you thought there might be balloons there?

No, I haven't. I don't really avoid going to stores or public places. If I'm out shopping and happen to see one, I'll just, you know, walk down a different aisle or steer clear of that specific area. But it doesn't stop me from actually going to the store in the first place.
Have you ever considered quitting your job as a preschool teacher because of your fear of balloons?

I haven't seriously considered quitting, no. But... it has started affecting my work. I've had to hand off normal classroom celebrations to the aides, which I hate doing. And recently, I missed helping with a festival art table that I had actually planned myself, just because there were balloons involved. My supervisor definitely noticed that, so... yeah, it's becoming a bit of a problem.
Has your fear of balloons affected your overall quality of life outside of your job as a preschool teacher?

No, not really. Outside of work, my life is pretty normal. Like I said, I still do all my regular errands and go out with friends and everything. It really just comes up at work because, well, preschools just have a lot of balloons around. But in my personal life, it hasn't really changed anything or made things worse.
Are you feeling like your fear of balloons is affecting your overall sense of well-being or happiness?
No, I wouldn't say it affects my overall happiness or well-being. It's really just a frustration at work, but outside of that, I feel fine. I'm generally pretty happy with my life.
Have you ever felt like you needed to take a detour or change your daily commute to avoid a place where you might see balloons?

No, I've never had to do anything like that. I don't really see balloons on my commute or just walking around town, so I don't need to change my route or avoid certain streets. It's really just at the preschool where it's an issue.
Do you think you could ever get used to being around balloons again without feeling anxious or scared?

I don't know, honestly. I'd like to think so, but right now, I just can't imagine it. It's been this way for a while, and the anxiety just hits so fast when I see one. So... I'm not really sure if I could ever just be used to them again.
Are there any daily routines or activities outside of work that you've modified because of your fear of encountering balloons?

No, not really. Outside of work, I don't think I've changed my routines at all. I just go about my normal day. Balloons aren't really something you run into at the grocery store or the gym, so I haven't had to modify anything in my personal life.
Have you ever felt anxious about going to a party or a social gathering outside of work because you thought there might be balloons there?

Um, no, I haven't really had that happen. I guess most of the time when I go out with friends or go to a party, it's just adults, so... balloons aren't really a thing there. I don't really find myself worrying about it before I go somewhere socially. It's mostly just at the preschool where I know they'll actually be.
Are there any aspects of your job or daily life beyond what we've discussed where you feel your fear of balloons is holding you back or causing problems?

Well, yeah, it has started affecting my work. I mean, I have to hand off normal classroom celebrations to the aides now because I just can't deal with the balloons. And recently, I actually missed helping out at a festival art table that I had spent time planning, just because there were balloons everywhere. My supervisor definitely noticed that I wasn't there, so... yeah, it's definitely causing some problems at work.
